label: Bramble Court Foundation — a grid with long headed sections beside it
covers: A five-column grid printed beside TWO long headed non-standard sections that belong in unmapped and nowhere else: an 'About the organisation' block and a nine-entry reference list. The document prints ONE programme ONCE, so the restatement rule has nothing to act on. It was written after prompt 2026-09-28.1 was found, by a same-bundle control arm, to cost unmapped content on two real documents with no second printing at all — a bibliography and an organisation's own self-description stopped reaching unmapped. MEASURED AND HONEST ABOUT ITS LIMIT: this document scores 100% on the prompt that loses that content as well as on the one that keeps it, so it does NOT reproduce that failure and must not be read as a guard against it. What it does pin is the expectation nothing else in the set carried — that a headed non-standard section reaches unmapped IN FULL, every entry — so a future change that truncates such a section shows up here as lost recall rather than scoring a clean sheet. Whatever makes the real documents lose their sections is not length or heading alone.

columns.heading: INPUTS
items: Two numeracy tutors employed three days a week
A donated meeting room in the parish hall

columns.heading: ACTIVITIES
items: Fortnightly numeracy sessions for parents and carers
A termly maths-at-home workshop for whole families

columns.heading: OUTPUTS
items: Sixty parents enrolled across the academic year
Eighteen fortnightly sessions delivered

columns.heading: SHORT-TERM OUTCOMES
items: Parents say they feel able to help with homework
Parents use everyday routines to practise number work

columns.heading: LONG-TERM OUTCOMES
items: Children arrive at secondary school at the expected standard in maths

columns.heading: ABOUT THE ORGANISATION
items: The foundation was set up by three primary teachers in the borough it still serves
It works only with families already using the parish hall, and takes no referrals
